run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T02:40:12Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy is returning 503s for a small but nonzero share of proxied requests. Its own span metric shows STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on operation 'ingress' (28.36 per hour, peak 10 per 5-minute bucket at ~02:35) and on 'router frontend egress' (6.08 per hour). The failing traces and Envoy access logs show the mechanism: the request reaches frontend-proxy's ingress, its egress call to the frontend returns no HTTP response (http.status_code=0, error=true) and Envoy logs '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' against upstream cluster 'frontend'; in those traces no frontend span exists at all, so the frontend application never produced a response. The same 503 UC pattern is present from at least 02:20:37 through 02:38:44 across many routes (/api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/recommendations), i.e. it is not a single new break but a recurring low-rate condition that existed before the 02:40:12 alert. The frontend pod itself is Ready, has never restarted, matches the Service's only endpoint, and its CPU/memory are not at hard saturation, so a crash, OOM, eviction or stale endpoint is not supported; the frontend also recorded its own error spans only in the 02:35 bucket (GET 5.56, POST 1.11, tcp.connect 1.11 per 5m), whose traces are outside Jaeger's retained window. A product-catalog rollout at 02:32:47-02:32:51 is a real change inside the window, but it is not supported as the cause: errors began before it, the new pod is Ready, logs 'Product Found' continuously, shows no error spans, and latency stayed flat. The exact trigger that makes the frontend terminate in-flight connections is not established, and the alert's reported value 0.0111 could not be reproduced from the available series (span-derived ratio at 02:40:12 is 0.000184), so the deepest cause remains unresolved.

claims.text: In the hour ending 2026-11-15T03:00:39Z, frontend-proxy emitted STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on exactly two operations: span_name 'ingress' 28.36 per hour and span_name 'router frontend egress' 6.08 per hour (increase over [1h]); no other frontend-proxy operation had an ERROR series.

frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans per 5-minute bucket were 2.28 at 02:15, 1.11 at 02:20, 2.22 at 02:25, 5.56 at 02:30, 10 at 02:35, 1.11 at 02:40, 0 at 02:45 and 3.33 at 02:50, against 2974-3119 ingress spans per bucket, i.e. an error share of roughly 0.04% to 0.33% with a peak in the 02:35 bucket.

Seven retained failing traces (02:20:37.764Z to 02:27:51.121Z) show the same shape: load-generator 'GET' span with error=true/http.status_code=503, child frontend-proxy 'ingress' span with http.status_code=503 and otel.status_code=ERROR, and child frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' span with error=true and http.status_code=0; those traces contain no frontend span, so the frontend application produced no response span for them.

frontend-proxy Envoy access logs record 503 with response flag 'UC' and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on 'GET /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4' at 02:33:41.331Z and 'GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO' at 02:38:44.723Z, with upstream cluster 'frontend' and upstream host '100.71.221.228:8080'.

The same '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' pattern occurs earlier than the 02:32 product-catalog rollout: '/api/recommendations?productIds=6E92ZMYYFZ' at 02:25:45.843Z, '/api/cart', '/api/products/HQTGWGPNH4' and '/api/data/?contextKeys=telescopes' at 02:26:02, '/api/products/9SIQT8TOJO' at 02:27:50.946Z and '/api/products/0PUK6V6EV0' at 02:28:49.036Z.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw is Running and Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-15T01:59:45Z, and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-mzj56 is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 01:59:46Z; the 'frontend' Service resolves to exactly one endpoint, 100.96.3.42:8080 targetRef frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw, which equals that pod's podIP, so no stale/mismatched endpoint is visible.

Container resources are tight on the frontend path: container 'frontend' has limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi and requests cpu 50m / memory 100Mi, and container 'frontend-proxy' has limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi.

The frontend container is CPU-throttled in 24.5% to 32.3% of CFS periods throughout 02:10-02:55 (highest value 0.3226 in the 02:35 bucket; 0.2448-0.2886 in the earlier buckets), while frontend-proxy is throttled in only 2.8% to 5.6% of periods; frontend CPU usage was 0.0457-0.0508 cores against its 0.1-core limit.
frontend memory working set rose steadily from 119,390,208 bytes at 02:10 to 130,891,776 bytes at 02:55 (limit 200Mi) with no drop or restart, and frontend-proxy stayed flat near 20.2-20.6 MB.

Latency did not degrade: frontend-proxy 'ingress' p95 was 567.8-605.4 ms in 02:15-02:25, 577.0 ms at 02:30, 631.9 ms at 02:35, 571.4 ms at 02:40 and 409.7-508.1 ms after, and the combined product-catalog GetProduct + frontend GET p95 stayed 82-114 ms (110.6 ms in the 02:35 bucket), so the failing 503s are too rare to show as a latency regression rather than a general slowdown.

The frontend service's own ERROR spans are confined to the 02:35 bucket: 'GET' 5.56 per 5m, 'POST' 1.11, 'POST /api/checkout' 1.11, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 1.11 and 'tcp.connect' 1.11; every other 5-minute bucket from 02:10 to 02:50 shows 0 for these operations, and no ERROR series was returned for grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder or AdService/GetAds.

product-catalog was replaced by its own controller inside the window: Deployment 'product-catalog' scaled up ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 (0->1) and down product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (1->0), with SuccessfulCreate of pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 at 02:32:47Z, container Start at 02:32:50Z and SuccessfulDelete of pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp at 02:32:51Z; the new pod is Running/Ready, restartCount 0, and logged 'Product Found' continuously from 02:33:17 onward.

No ERROR-status span series was returned for product-catalog in the hour aggregate (its only series are STATUS_CODE_UNSET), while the only other ERROR series in the namespace belong to long-lived flagd streaming spans on ad (3.05/h 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream'), fraud-detection (3.04/h) and recommendation (4.05/h '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream'), not to request handling of this alert's path.

The span-derived frontend-proxy error ratio at the alert's firing instant 2026-11-15T02:40:12Z over a 5-minute window is 0.0001838 (sum of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans / all frontend-proxy spans), which does not equal the 0.01111111111111111 stated in the alert annotation.

Primary mechanism hypothesis: frontend-proxy's 503s are caused by the frontend application terminating in-flight HTTP connections before responding (Envoy 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}', egress http.status_code=0, no frontend span in the trace); because the alert triggers on an error rate above 0, this recurring low-rate reset condition is enough to fire it. What makes the frontend drop those requests is not proven; sustained CPU throttling of the frontend container at its 100m limit (24.5-32.3% of CFS periods, peaking at 32.3% in the 02:35 bucket) is the leading contributing candidate, but the flat p95 aggregates show no correlated latency regression and this remains correlation only.

Alternative unresolved hypothesis: an upstream keep-alive/idle-timeout mismatch between frontend-proxy's Envoy cluster and the frontend HTTP server could produce exactly this sporadic 'connection_termination' reset that disappears on retry (one trace, 8bd647d2c7c1d1786a4a40e6b1c89f2f, contains a failed 503 ingress span followed by a successful 200 ingress span with a complete frontend chain); frontend-proxy's Envoy configuration is not exposed as a ConfigMap in otel-demo (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products exist), so the timeout settings could not be verified.

The 02:32:47-02:32:51 product-catalog rollout is rejected as the cause of the frontend-proxy alert: frontend-proxy 503 UC resets and ERROR spans are documented from 02:20:37, before that rollout; the replacement pod is Ready with 0 restarts and serves 'Product Found' without error spans; and product-catalog/frontend p95 latency stayed flat (82-114 ms) across the rollout.

A frontend pod failure (crash, OOM, eviction, or stale endpoint) is not supported: the frontend pod has restartCount 0, is Ready, generated no Kubernetes events in the window, matches the single Service endpoint 100.96.3.42:8080, and its memory working set (131 MB vs 200Mi limit) and CPU usage (about 0.05 of a 0.1-core limit) show no hard saturation or OOM mark.

gaps: The alerting rule itself is not retrievable: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name 'RequestErrorRate' and no alerting rules at all for type=alert, so the expression and label set that produced 'current: 0.01111111111111111' are unknown; the available span-derived ratio at the firing instant is 0.0001838, so the alert value could not be reproduced or reconciled.

Jaeger coverage for this problem ends before the alert: the newest frontend trace returned was at 2026-11-15T02:28:42.907Z and the newest frontend-proxy 503 trace at 02:27:51.121Z, so the 02:35 error peak (where the frontend's own GET/POST/tcp.connect error spans occur) cannot be inspected at trace level, and the frontend span status codes/details behind those 02:35 errors are unknown.

The frontend container produced no readable stdout/stderr lines in 02:30-02:45 (0 bytes read on both the current and previous instance), so there is no application-log evidence of what the frontend did or why it terminated connections; the trigger on the frontend side remains unknown.
No frontend runtime/GC metrics are available for this pod: v8js_memory_heap_used_bytes returned only for pod otel-collector, so event-loop stall/GC pressure on the Node frontend could not be tested.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_available and kube_pod_container_info returned no series for otel-demo in the window, so deployment-level availability history and image digests during the incident could not be verified.

frontend-proxy's Envoy bootstrap/cluster configuration is not present as a ConfigMap in otel-demo, and secrets cannot be read, so upstream idle timeouts, retry policy and max_requests_per_connection could not be checked.
The replaced product-catalog pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp no longer exists, so its logs around 02:32:47-02:32:51 are unavailable; its behaviour at deletion is unknown.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so change records other than Kubernetes events (e.g. who triggered the product-catalog rollout at 02:32:47 and whether any frontend/config change preceded the 02:20 onset) are unknown.
next_steps: Retrieve the actual RequestErrorRate alert rule expression and its evaluation window from the alerting stack, to confirm which metric/labels produce the reported 0.01111111111111111 and whether the alert is intentionally 'fires on any nonzero error' at very low traffic slices.

Compare frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream cluster settings (idle_timeout, max_requests_per_connection, retry policy) against the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive timeout, since a reuse race is a plausible explanation for sporadic 'UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' events.

Capture frontend application logs (currently not surfaced on stdout) for the 02:30-02:45 period, and retain/inspect traces from the 02:35 peak to identify the frontend-side reason behind the GET/POST/tcp.connect error spans.

Evaluate raising the frontend container CPU limit above 100m (observed 0.05 cores used with 24.5-32.3% of CFS periods throttled) and adding retries on the frontend-proxy egress cluster for idempotent GET routes.
Confirm whether the 02:32:47 product-catalog rollout was an intentional configuration change (same image digest) and record it as a separate change event rather than as this alert's cause.
